k1845:
A studio at Shkëmbi i Kavajës, on the rail side of the area, that has been partitioned to work as a 1+1.

The flat measures 50 m² gross and 44 m² net, and holds a living room with the kitchen, a separate bedroom and a bathroom. It sits on the third floor of a new building with a lift.

The division is what makes the difference at this size: a studio and a one-bedroom flat of the same square metres live very differently, and this one closes the bedroom door.

The sea and the main services are both close. The seller is open to discussing the price.
k1846: 2+1 apartment with a separate kitchen and store room, Vala Park
k1847: A two-bedroom flat at Vala Park with a kitchen in its own room and a separate store, about 80 m² in all.
k1848:
A 2+1 apartment at Vala Park, a quiet and well-served part of Durrës.

The certificate records 60 m²; with the addition the flat comes to around 80 m². It holds two bedrooms, a living room, a bathroom, a store room and — unusually for this market — a kitchen in a room of its own rather than opening off the living space.

A separate kitchen is a matter of taste, but for anyone who cooks properly it is the detail that decides between two otherwise similar flats. The store room takes what a flat of this size normally has nowhere to put.

It is on the first floor. Schools, markets, transport and the everyday services are all close, and the ownership certificate is in order.
k1849: Front-line 1+1 apartment with a full sea view, Golem
k1850: A 78 m² one-bedroom flat on the Golem seafront with an uninterrupted sea view and a guaranteed parking space.
k1851:
A 1+1 apartment on the front line at Golem, with the sea directly in front of it.

The flat measures 78 m² — generous for this layout — and holds a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom and a bathroom. It is on the second floor.

The view is the whole argument here: it runs unbroken to the water, with nothing built between the flat and the shore. On this coast that is a diminishing commodity, since the second line keeps filling in.

A parking space comes with it, which in season is worth more than it sounds. The ownership history is in order and the purchase can be financed with a mortgage.
k1852: 2+1 apartment 30 m from the sea, Plazh, Durrës
k1853: A 91 m² flat laid out as a 2+1, thirty metres from the shore, with a dedicated parking space and camera security.
k1854:
An apartment at Plazh laid out as a 2+1, thirty metres from the shore.

The certificate records 91 m², arranged as a living room with the kitchen, sleeping rooms and a bathroom. The flat is on the fifth floor and the building has a lift.

Thirty metres is as close as this coast gets without being on the sand itself — near enough that the beach is part of daily life rather than an outing.

The building has camera security and the flat comes with a parking space of its own. The ownership certificate is in order, and the position suits living here year round as much as using it for the summer.
k1855: Three 1+1 flats and an office unit sold together, Plazh
k1856: An income package at Plazh: three one-bedroom flats and an office unit on the first floor, 114 m² on the certificate, sold only as a whole.
k1857:
Three 1+1 apartments and an office unit at Plazh, on the first floor, offered as a single lot.

The certificate records 114 m² across the four. They are sold only together — the seller will not break the package up, which is worth knowing before viewing.

What this is, in practice, is a small rental business rather than a home. Three flats let separately, plus commercial space that can be let on its own terms or used to run the operation from.

The ownership certificate is in order. The position is close to the sea and to the everyday services, which is what keeps units of this size occupied both in and out of season.
k1858: Well-furnished 1+1 apartment 200 m from the sea, Plazh
k1859: A 77 m² one-bedroom flat on the fifth floor at Plazh, facing south-east, furnished and ready, with resident parking.
k1860:
A 1+1 apartment at Plazh, two hundred metres from the sea.

The flat measures 77 m² gross and 67 m² net: a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom and a bathroom, on the fifth floor of a building with a lift.

It has been furnished with care rather than filled, and is ready to live in as it stands. The south-east orientation brings the light in early and keeps the flat out of the worst of the afternoon heat — which through an Albanian August is not a small thing.

The building has an administrator and parking for residents. The seller is open to discussing the price.
k1861: Studio on the fourth floor, Golem
k1862: A 41 m² studio at Golem, close to the sea and the everyday services, on the fourth floor.
k1863:
A studio at Golem, one of the most popular holiday areas on this stretch of coast.

The flat measures 41 m² gross and 35 m² net, arranged as a living room with the kitchen and a bathroom, on the fourth floor.

At this size the layout does the work, and here the space has been organised so the sleeping and living areas do not fight each other.

The sea and the main services are both a short walk away. A studio in Golem is bought about as often as a summer base as it is to let by the week.
k1864: 301 m² floor with a project for nine studios, opposite the station
k1865: A 301 m² property opposite the Sports Palace and the railway station, with a drawn-up scheme for nine studios and a laundry.
k1866:
A large property in Durrës facing the Sports Palace and the railway station, sold as a development rather than as a home.

It covers 301 m² in total with 274 m² of internal space, on the third residential floor, reached by stairs.

A scheme has already been drawn up for what to do with it: nine studios and a laundry room, which is the shape an apart-hotel or a short-let operation takes. The seller will sell it as it stands or finished to that plan, and which of those a buyer wants changes the sum entirely.

The position is the reason the scheme works. Arriving passengers step off the train within sight of the building, and everything the centre of Durrës offers is a short walk away.
k1867: Unfurnished studio near Hotel Miki, Plazh Iliria
k1868: A 28 m² studio on the third floor at Plazh Iliria, sold empty so the fit-out can be chosen by the buyer.
k1869:
A studio in the Iliria part of Plazh, near Hotel Miki, on the third floor of a building with a lift.

The flat measures 28 m² in total with 23 m² net: a living room with the kitchen and a bathroom.

It is sold empty. That is worth weighing rather than glossing over — it means an outlay before the flat can be used or let, but it also means the fit-out is chosen rather than inherited, which for a short-let flat decides how it photographs.

The ownership certificate is in order. The sea and the services of Plazh are both close, and small flats in this pocket let readily through the season.
k1870: Tenanted commercial unit, Plazh Hekurudha, Durrës
k1871: An 88 m² commercial unit at Plazh Hekurudha, currently let to an estate agency at €500 net a month.
k1872:
A commercial unit at Plazh Hekurudha, sold with a tenant already in it.

The internal area is 54 m², the card records 34 m², and the total comes to 88 m².

The unit is currently let to an estate agency at €500 net a month, so the income starts on the day the sale completes rather than whenever a tenant is found. For an investor that removes the gap that usually follows a purchase — though the terms of the existing lease are worth reading before signing anything.

The position is a good one within Plazh Hekurudha, and the space suits a range of businesses should the current tenancy end.
k1873: 1+1 apartment on the sixth floor, Plazh Iliria
k1874: A 55 m² one-bedroom flat at Plazh Iliria, in a well-run building with a lift, close to the sea.
k1875:
A 1+1 apartment at Plazh Iliria, one of the parts of the Durrës beach area that people return to.

The certificate records 55 m²: a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom and a bathroom, on the sixth floor of a building with a lift.

The building is well run, which is worth more in a seaside block than in a city one — the common parts take a beating through the season, and it shows quickly when nobody is looking after them.

The layout is straightforward and the sea and the main services are both close by.
k1877: A 117 m² three-bedroom flat on the fifth floor at Plazh; the building has no lift.
k1878:
A 3+1 apartment at Plazh, large enough to house a family without compromise.

The certificate records 116.5 m²: three bedrooms, a living room with the kitchen and a bathroom, on the fifth residential floor.

The building has no lift. At the fifth floor with three bedrooms that is the thing to settle first, and it is reflected in what the flat costs against comparable ones nearby.

What it buys is space — three separate bedrooms in this area, at this price, is not a common combination. The rooms hold daylight through the day, and the sea and the main services are both within reach.
k1879: 1+1 apartment in Turquoise Marina, Gjiri i Lalëzit
k1880: A 70 m² one-bedroom flat in a marina resort at Gjiri i Lalëzit, with a private beach, pools and boat moorings.
k1881:
A 1+1 apartment in Turquoise Marina at Gjiri i Lalëzit, one of the largest resort developments on the Albanian coast.

The flat measures 69.9 m² gross and 60.8 m² net: a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom and a bathroom, on the second floor.

What is being bought here is the complex as much as the flat. There is a private beach, a pool and an aquapark, a harbour with moorings for boats, bars and restaurants inside the grounds, dedicated parking, cycle paths and sports facilities — and it is possible to move around parts of the development by water.

Gjiri i Lalëzit sits away from the busier stretches of the Durrës coast, which is the point of it: the development supplies what the surroundings do not.
k1882: Furnished 1+1 apartment with balcony near the hospital, Durrës
k1883: A 65 m² one-bedroom flat on the fourth floor near the hospital, sold furnished exactly as photographed.
k1884:
A 1+1 apartment near the hospital in Durrës, in a part of the city that is easy to reach from anywhere in it.

The certificate records 65 m²: a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom, a bathroom and a balcony, on the fourth floor.

The flat is sold furnished exactly as it appears in the photographs, which is worth saying plainly — it means what is shown is what is included, with nothing to be removed before handover.

The surrounding area is settled and residential, and the main services are within easy reach. It works as a home or as something held and let.
k1886: An 83 m² two-bedroom flat on the second floor in Lagjja 16, restored throughout, with a balcony.
k1887:
A 2+1 apartment in Lagjja 16, on the second floor above the ground in an established building.

The net area is 83 m². Inside there are two bedrooms, a living room with the kitchen, a bathroom, a balcony and a distribution corridor that keeps the rooms off one another.

The flat has been fully restored, so what it offers is the layout and the position of an older building with the condition of a new one — which is often the better bargain, since the bones of these blocks tend to be more generous than what gets built now.

The quarter is quiet and suited to family living, and the low floor keeps the stairs short.
k1888: 1+1 apartment with a 12.5 m² green balcony, Golem
k1889: A 44 m² one-bedroom flat on the first floor at Golem with a private planted balcony, furnished and equipped, offered as an urgent sale.
k1890:
A 1+1 apartment at Golem on the first floor, with a private balcony of 12.5 m² that has been planted rather than left bare.

The certificate records 44 m²: a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom and a bathroom.

The flat is fully furnished and equipped — white goods in place, air conditioning installed, the bathroom new. Nothing needs spending on it before it can be used or let.

On a flat this size the balcony effectively adds a room for most of the year, which is the argument for this one over a larger flat without outdoor space. The seller is looking for a quick sale.
k1891: 620 m² plot near University Road, Spitallë
